title: Spatially Resolved Water Emission from Gravitationally Lensed Dusty Star-forming Galaxies at z ∼ 3
question: Does L_H2O (p-H2O 2_{0,2}-1_{1,1}) correlate with L_FIR on resolved ~kpc scales in lensed high-z dusty star-forming galaxies, and can it serve as a resolved SFR calibrator?

what.value: Magnifications and 870 um lens models/source sizes for SPT sources

evidence.quote: Magnification ($\mu$) of the SPT sources are taken from ALMA 870 $\mu$m lens models (cite: spilker16).

what.value: Local and high-z literature H2O luminosities and L_FIR samples

evidence.quote: The local sample is drawn from the *Herschel* Science Archive (cite: yang13)
spatially and spectrally resolved observations of mid$-$J CO$(6-5)$ in SPT0529-54, SPT0532-50 (cite: dong19)
The gas mass values from (cite: bothwell17) (estimated using \[CI\] observations) in SPT0529-54 and SPT0532-50

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image continuum and line cubes
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration; CASA clean with natural weighting and tapers; continuum from line-free data; cubes at 50/100 km/s

recipe.goal: Fit dust SED to get L_FIR
recipe.method: Modified blackbody with MCMC to unresolved photometry, rest-frame >=50 um, beta fixed to 2; free amplitude, T_d, lambda_0
Scale total L_FIR by each pixel's fraction of the continuum flux
assumptions: uniform dust temperature and opacity across source

recipe.method: Apply continuum mask to each channel, integrate; error = std of line-free channels; non-parametric second-moment FWHM; L_H2O from Solomon & Vanden Bout relation; per-pixel from moment 0

recipe.goal: Fit L_H2O-L_FIR correlation global and resolved
recipe.method: MCMC fits of log L_H2O vs log L_FIR including literature; slope-fixed-to-zero fit of ratio; resolved pixels binned in Sigma_LFIR; F-test between free and fixed slope
assumptions: H2O and FIR co-spatially lensed; differential lensing negligible

recipe.goal: Calibrate SFR and test dependence on physical properties
recipe.method: SFR=1.47e-10 L_IR (Kennicutt & Evans), L_IR/L_FIR~1.38; compare ratio vs lambda_max, Sigma_gas, tau_100; compare with CO(6-5)

evidence.quote: we estimate $\rm \tau_{100}$ $\sim$0.34, 1.36 and 0.46 for SPT0529-54, SPT0532-50 and SPT0538-54 respectively

not_stated_but_needed: Number of clean iterations, threshold and clean mask details
Exact line-free channel ranges used for continuum and rms
Spectral window handling/continuum subtraction method for the cubes
Pixel size values and image sizes
Priors and number of walkers/steps in the emcee fits (SED and L_H2O-L_FIR)
Flux calibrators and flux scale uncertainty
Binning details for resolved correlation and how the F-test was implemented
Whether primary beam correction was applied
missing_for_reproduction: CLEAN parameters, line-free channels, pixel sizes
score_reason: Data public and equations given, but imaging and fitting settings are incomplete.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric results (ratio, SFR calibration), reasonably clear recipe.
